detection_signals.reasoning: A single source IP (198.51.100.207) attempted 23 login requests against the /login endpoint in just 3.36 seconds, resulting in 6 failed logins spanning 6 distinct usernames. This targeted rotation of multiple usernames from one IP indicates automated credential stuffing/brute force behavior.

assessment_at_capture.rationale: The incident shows a deliberate, high-speed attack pattern from a single source IP (198.51.100.207) with a known malicious reputation for brute-force and scanning activity. Crucially, the attack resulted in 5 successful logins across multiple distinct target usernames within a very brief time window of 3.36 seconds. This represents a clearly successful large-scale compromise attempt, fulfilling the criteria for Critical severity and requiring immediate on-call escalation.

correlation.intel_summary: Threat intelligence lookup on the sole source IP '198.51.100.207' returned a 'malicious' reputation categorized as a scanner, specifically associated with known host-scanning and brute-force activity ranges.
correlation.enrichment_notes: The IP 198.51.100.207 is confirmed as malicious (known host-scanning / brute-force source range). Combined with the fact that this IP successfully authenticated 5 times across multiple distinct target usernames (alice, bob, netdisco, etc.) within a very short burst of activity (23 requests in ~3.4 seconds), this elevates the incident from a simple automated scan to a severe credential stuffing or brute-force attack with confirmed successful compromises.
